newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lend Lease confident on Darling Park.
newsitem.headline: Lend Lease confident on Darling Park.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd said on Thursday it was confident about the long term prospects of its Darling Park office project in Sydney.
Asked at a news conference what impact the Darling Park project would have on the company's future earnings, Lend Lease managing director David Higgins said: "It's early days yet."
"We are extremely confident of this asset. I think you have to look first at the underlying asset," he said.
Higgins said Lend Lease saw the major growth in the Australian commercial property market as being in Sydney.
"The proof is in the last boom, the two major corporate leasing deals happened at Darling Park and they were done at levels that were exactly related to levels to deals done in the city," he said.
Higgins said development funds were new to the market and, consequently, not very well understood by the market.
These types of funds were speculative investments and gave a higher rate of return than the traditional property trust, Higgins said.
"It has a three year time frame before you have an indication of how successful any of these things are," he said.
The Darling Park Trust units listed in December last year at A$1, the same price as their issue price.
Unitholders are required to pay a further installment of A$1.50 due on December 31, 1999 to raise a further A$195 million.

Funds from the issue will be used to acquire a 50 percent stake in the existing 27 story IBM Tower at Darling Park and fund a 50 percent involvement in the development of stage two of the Darling Park project.

The project is currently owned 30 percent by Lend Lease, and 7.5 percent by Japanese company Toyo Real Estate Co and 12.5 percent by a unit of Nomura Securities with the remaining 50 percent owned by the trust.
At 1.35 p.m (0235 GMT), Darling Park Trust units were one cent weaker at 84 cents.
